title: Minkä näköisiä: asking about several people's or things' appearance
summary: For several people or things, use minkä näköisiä. Minkä näköisiä talot ovat? — Talot ovat korkeita.
targetSkills: Minkä näköisiä: asking about several people's or things' appearance
prerequisiteSkills: Minkä näköinen: asking about one person's or thing's appearance
objectives: Ask about several people's or things' appearance with minkä näköisiä.
Describe the visible quality using a plural partitive adjective.

sections.title: Meaning and pattern
paragraphs: Plural means more than one in this grammatical pattern.
A stem is the part of a word to which an ending is attached.
The partitive is a word form used here for an amount, an action's object, or a substance or group description.
The genitive is a relationship form; in these question phrases minkä means of what or which.
For several people or things, use minkä näköisiä. Minkä stays unchanged and näköinen takes the plural partitive form näköisiä. Minkänäköisiä is an equivalent joined spelling.
keyPoints: Do not leave näköinen singular when asking about the members of these plural groups.

sections.title: Answering the question
paragraphs: Give the visible characteristic with a plural partitive adjective: Talot ovat korkeita (“The houses are tall”). These ordinary groups use the same descriptive number pattern as earlier plural descriptions. The complete taught adjective forms are explained and supplied where formation is supporting context.
A natural short reply to “Minkä näköisiä talot ovat?” is “Korkeita.” (“Tall.”). Use the full reply when it makes the person, action or correction clearer.
A negative appearance correction retains the ordinary plural descriptive pattern. The complete phrase eivät ole rejects the wrong appearance; the next sentence gives the actual visible quality.
The exercises show supporting Finnish words and their meanings when recalling them is not the task. Read the complete English meaning before choosing the question or answer form.
keyPoints: Use a plural describing form for the appearance of these groups.

sections.title: Build the answer forms
paragraphs: korkeita means tall here. Korkea uses the plural stem korkei- with -ta: korkeita.
pitkiä means tall here. Pitkä changes final ä to i and adds ä: pitkiä.
punaisia means red here. Punainen changes -nen to -sia: punaisia.
pieniä means small here. Pieni has the taught plural partitive pieniä; add -ä to this surface pattern.
suuria means large here. Suuri has the taught plural partitive suuria; add -a to this surface pattern.
mustia means black here. Musta changes final a to i and adds a: mustia.
pyöreitä means round here. Pyöreä uses the plural stem pyörei- with -tä: pyöreitä.
ruskeita means brown here. Ruskea uses the plural stem ruskei- with -ta: ruskeita.
sinisiä means blue here. Sininen changes -nen to -siä: sinisiä.
vihreitä means green here. Vihreä uses the taught plural stem vihrei- with -tä: vihreitä.
valkoisia means white here. Valkoinen changes -nen to -sia: valkoisia.
keyPoints: Use a plural describing form for the appearance of these groups.
